function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content: Electricity as a natural phenomenon has been known for millennia—ancient Greeks like Thales of Miletus observed static sparks from amber. The systematic scientific discovery and naming of the phenomenon began in the 16th‑17th centuries with William Gilbert, who coined the term “electricus” and distinguished magnetism from static electricity. Subsequent breakthroughs came from Benjamin Franklin (the lightning‑rod experiment), Alessandro Volta (inventing the voltaic pile), and many others who built on Gilbert’s work to develop our modern understanding of electrical currents and circuits.
